title: Check yourself: what Q2 does with your QBeans

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A KeyRotation QBean extends QBeanSupport and has a setIntervalHours(int) method, but no interface of its own. Its descriptor contains <attr name="intervalHours" type="int">12</attr>. What does Q2 do with the file?

options.text: It deploys the bean with the descriptor's value, since without an interface of its own QFactory calls setIntervalHours by reflection
options.says: Q2 never calls the method directly; it sets the attribute through the MBean server

options.text: It deploys the bean with its own default, since without an interface of its own QFactory skips an attribute it can't map
options.says: an unknown attribute is not skipped: AttributeNotFoundException fails the deploy

options.text: It renames the file .BAD, since without an interface of its own the MBean server sees only QBeanSupportMBean's attributes
options.says: without an interface of its own the bean exposes QBeanSupportMBean, which has no IntervalHours, so the deploy fails

options.text: It renames the file .ENV, since without an interface of its own the MBean server rejects the bean with an Error
options.says: the bean registers through QBeanSupportMBean; the unknown attribute is an exception, and an exception while deploying renames the file .BAD

origin.section: 14.4 `<attr>` Is Set Through JMX, So Its Setter Belongs in the MBean Interface

questions.stem: A FeeTable QBean loads its fee file in initService. On Monday the file is missing, initService throws, and Q2 logs a warning. An hour later an operator copies the file into place and calls start on the bean from JConsole. What happens?

options.text: The bean starts and loads the fees, since start runs again whatever step failed before
options.says: start does not run initService; it checks the state, and a bean whose init never completed is not startable

options.text: The bean starts without any fees, since start goes on without the step it missed
options.says: start returns without doing anything for a bean whose init never completed, so the bean does not start at all

options.text: The bean stays Unknown, since start returns at once for a bean whose init never completed
options.says: QBeanSupport.start only runs from Stopped, Failed or Destroyed; the bean stays Unknown and only a redeploy brings it back

options.text: The bean becomes Failed, since start refuses a bean whose init never completed
options.says: Failed means startService threw; for a bean whose init never completed start returns at once and the state stays Unknown

origin.section: 14.3 A Configuration Refused in `setConfiguration` Renames the File; Refused Later, It Only Logs

questions.stem: After a restart, 20_scoring.xml deploys a QBean whose startService waits up to 10 seconds for risk-model, a name that 60_model.xml registers in its own startService. Both files are in deploy/ before Q2 starts. What does the first pass do?

options.text: The scoring bean starts once the model registers, since the model's start runs on its own thread during the wait
options.says: Q2 calls the starts one after another on one thread, so the model's start can't run during the wait

options.text: The scoring bean starts after the model does, since Q2 sees the wait and starts 60_model.xml ahead of it
options.says: Q2 starts in file order and does not reorder; the scoring bean's start blocks the pass

options.text: The scoring bean is Failed after its wait, since the model's start can only begin once that wait has ended
options.says: the wait runs on Q2's thread, so 60_model.xml starts only after it; the scoring bean fails and every later start is 10 seconds late

options.text: The scoring bean is Started after its wait, since Q2 starts 60_model.xml while that wait runs
options.says: Q2 calls the starts one after another on one thread, so 60_model.xml starts only after the wait, too late; the scoring bean is Failed

origin.section: 14.5 Nothing Is Started Until Everything Is Initialised, So a QBean Looks for What It Needs in `startService`

questions.stem: A deployment script writes 40_acquirer_channel.xml straight into the deploy directory of a running server, and now and then the file ends up renamed .BAD although the descriptor inside it is valid. Which change to the script stops this?

options.text: Write the file in another directory on the same file system and move it in, since Q2 parses a new file at once
options.says: Q2 reads a new file as soon as it appears; a move within one file system is a rename, so Q2 sees no file or the whole one

options.text: Write the file in another directory on another file system and move it in, since Q2 trusts only files it did not see created
options.says: across file systems a move is a copy, which Q2 can again see half-written; ATOMIC_MOVE refuses it, and Q2 has no notion of trusted files

options.text: Write the file straight into deploy/ through deployElement, since Q2 waits for a file that it writes itself
options.says: deployElement writes the file in place with a FileWriter, so it has the same exposure once Q2 is watching

options.text: Write the file straight into deploy/ as a transient one, since Q2 holds back a file carrying its instance id
options.says: a transient descriptor only carries the instance id so it is deleted at exit or by the next Q2; it is read as soon as it appears like any other

origin.section: 14.6 Q2 Deploys Whatever It Finds in `deploy/`, Even Half a File

concepts: An attr element is set through the MBean server, so the setter must be in the bean's MBean interface or the file is .BAD, and a value changed over JMX lasts until the next redeploy.
Q2 reads a new file as soon as it appears, so a descriptor written in place can be renamed .BAD half-written; write it elsewhere and move it in.
A bean whose init threw is Unknown and start does nothing for it, while a bean whose start threw is Failed and can be started again.
Starts run one after another on Q2's thread in file order, so a wait in startService can't let a provider in a later file start, and it delays every start after it.
